## Paper

Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning

## World

cross_world_methods

## Institution

Not applicable: method paper.

## Agent type

Deep Q-network / value-based neural RL.

## Theoretical benchmark

Method benchmark: neural Q-learning with replay, a target network, and TD-error minimization.

## Learning setup

Structured observations encoded as vectors, epsilon-greedy exploration, replay buffer sampling, target-network bootstrapping, and a neural Q function.

## Metrics

Repo-side: finite task metrics, smoke/full outputs, DQN-vs-tabular comparisons, and tests for replay/target-network behavior.

## Main result

The DQN agent achieved human-level performance across a diverse set of 49 games using end-to-end reinforcement learning without handcrafted features.

## What they prove

The stability and effectiveness of the DQN algorithm with experience replay, target networks, and Huber TD loss in deep reinforcement learning.

## What they only simulate

The results are based on simulation of Atari 2600 games and do not include real-world empirical validation.

## What they do NOT test

The paper does not test the algorithm on real-world economic or social environments beyond the simulated games.

## What we need to reproduce

Do not reproduce Atari for this thesis. Reproduce the DQN method obligation: neural Q-values, target network, replay buffer, agent-local randomness, TD/Huber loss, and cross-world validation from minds/deep_rl/torch_dqn_mind.py; Phase 3 and Resource Island DQN tests..

## How our project differs

The paper validates DQN on high-dimensional game inputs. This repo adapts the DQN update structure to structured economic observations and tests whether it changes economic behavior relative to tabular Q-learning.

## Implementation obligations

Fixed-width feature encoder; Q-network; target Q-network; replay memory; epsilon-greedy exploration from an agent-local RNG; TD/Huber loss; target-network sync; finite-value guards.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

minds/deep_rl/torch_dqn_mind.py; test_phase3_deep_rl.py; Resource Island Phase 3 tests; outputs/phase3_full/mind_comparison.csv; cross-world ladder outputs.

## Failure modes to audit

DQN label without replay or target network; global shared RNG that collapses independent agents; smoke-only evidence; comparing DQN to tabular Q without confirming the observation encoder is meaningful.

## Project code comparison

Compare Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning to minds/deep_rl/torch_dqn_mind.py and minds/deep_rl/torch_dqn_mind.py; Phase 3 and Resource Island DQN tests.. The repo should claim DQN as an adapted method baseline, not as an Atari reproduction.
